findings.reason: §2's done-when ("a grep of `reckon/` finds no read of a moved field except through the accessor") cannot be met while `argv` has two writers, and the cheaper change is to extend the spec the plan does not mention.
findings.text: §2 says "dispatch-time detail that no live reader consults moves from the pointer into a file in the run's directory, written once at dispatch" and lists `argv` among the fields it moves, but `SUPERVISOR_SPEC_NAME = "supervisor.json"` is already that file: `_supervisor_spec` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2023`) composes it at dispatch, `_launch_supervisor_spec` writes it into the run directory (:2282), it carries `plan.argv`, `cwd`, `environment`, `prompt_path`, `worktree` and `attempt`, and it already has a single reader that answers "read the spec, else nothing" — the move-and-read-through-an-accessor shape §2 describes. `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2645` and `:2951`/`:3045` already re-export it for other callers, so a second dispatch-time run-directory file beside it means two files carrying the same argv and two readers to keep in step.

findings.reason: an author who sees the twelve sites and the two existing projections in one pass writes the census into §2 instead of discovering it in the first implementation node.
findings.text: §2 places its one accessor here, and the plan names no owner for the fields it moves, so the "one accessor in `reckon/crew/runs.py`" has no census. The live-pointer read sites §2 would have to route are `reckon/run_record.py:159` (`promoted_picker_selection`), `reckon/crew/promotion.py:902` and `:1436`, `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:138`, `:747` and `:1323` (the latter a *write* of `admit_request`), `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1172`, `reckon/serve.py:645` (`argv`), `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:933`, `reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py:466`, `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:224` and `reckon/crew/picker/outcomes.py:360` — twelve sites across nine files outside `runs.py`. Worse, `unreconciled_override` and `picker_selection` are already projected by `reckon/run_store.py:21` (`DETAIL_FIELDS`, "the wide fields a rotation may remove") and carried on the ledger row by `reckon/ledger.py:189`, so the field §2 moves is under three mechanisms at once and the plan reconciles none of them.

findings.reason: naming the owner turns §7's done-when into a call on an existing installer rather than a second one, and the plan's own reuse map then has an entry.
findings.text: §7's "hourly user timer, the same arrangement as `reckon-paid-lanes.timer`" cites the *instance* and not the owner: `render_timer_unit` (`reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py:1334`) and `install_timer` (`:1341`) are the code that renders and installs a service-plus-timer pair under `service.systemd_user_dir()` via `service.write_named_unit`, with the idempotent "write only when the definition changed, then daemon-reload and enable --now" behaviour already implemented. §7's "the unit files install the timer at an hourly interval" leaves the owner unnamed, and `reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:315` is a third unit renderer in the same tree.

findings.reason: the section gains a one-line dependency on the existing rotating writer, and its node stops re-deriving a rotation it can lean on.
findings.text: §7 says a pass "appends its removals to one log under the crew home, which rotates at a fixed size". That writer exists: `WATCH_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (`reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:744`), the rotation class `_WatchLogStream` at `:795` with `_rotate_if_needed` (`:852`), and its docstring already records the two hazards the plan's log would have to solve — a library holding a descriptor across a rename writes to the rotated-away inode, and the redirection has to survive rotation. `reckon/serve.py:317` is a second precedented rotation. §7 adds a third without saying why neither can be reused.

findings.reason: the plan's §6 predicate and the existing bound must be reconciled or the exit-path removal silently fights the gc bound over the same paths.
findings.text: §6 says of the `cache/` tree "nothing reads either after the process ends" and "Nothing removes them at any other time", but the directory is already bounded in the same `gc` loop §3 modifies: `bound_run_files` (`reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:1006`, called from `reckon/crew/gc.py:572`) bounds every over-limit file under the run directory against `run_file_limit_bytes` (`fleet_supervisor.py:1108`, `flight.run_file_max_mb`), and `reckon/crew/gc.py:57` (`_HARNESS_SCRATCH_DIRS = {"codex-home", "harness"}`) already classifies `codex-home` as harness scratch — the same two trees §6 names. §6 removes them at exit instead, so the run directory has two owners of its size and the plan states neither the interaction nor which one stops.

findings.reason: naming the flight key and the merge target (§2 into `supervisor.json`) is the accounting the item asks for, and it is a one-line addition per section.
findings.text: public_definitions 2030, cli_options 402, mcp_views 19, refusal_families 23. Measured over the section text: §3 accounts for its own surface (it replaces the thirty-day age and drops the dated subdirectories it first proposed) and is the only section that does. §7 adds a new systemd unit pair, a third log format with a fixed-size rotation, and a per-pass removal cap; §2 adds a second kind of run-directory sidecar and an accessor; neither names what it retires or merges, and §7's cap and interval become new tunable surface beside `flight.run_file_max_mb` and `raw_report_retention_days` (`reckon/flight.py:978`). §3's grace window is declared "in flight config" without naming the key, so it too adds a public config name the section does not account for.
